description: Compact rendered numerical summaries for package documentation. Full observations and numerical regeneration are maintained in the analysis repository.

blocks.text:
Measured **prusie 0.3.0** against **susieR 0.16.6** on the same inputs.

| Evaluated cases | Cases | Runtime ratio | Fitting-stage ratio | Median peak-memory ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GWAS | 200 | 42.9× | 48.1× | 5.11× |
| eQTL | 14,157 | 26.6× | 29.8× | 4.60× |

The runtime ratios divide the summed susieR time by the summed prusie time, using each case's median of three retained complete calls, with one numerical thread; the fitting stage excludes input and LD preparation. The memory ratio is the median of paired susieR/prusie ratios of peak backend-process memory. All measurements are from exclusive AMD EPYC 7742 nodes. Ratios for other traits, tissues, region sizes and LD references may differ; see [performance](https://lucajiang.github.io/prusie/performance.html).

The fixed panel contains **200 FinnGen R13 type 2 diabetes GWAS loci** (n = 486,019; 89,727 cases and 396,292 controls) and **14,157 GTEx v11 Whole_Blood genes** (n = 800). GWAS is fitted with the Gaussian RSS approximation. Every case is included, including iteration-limit fits and cases with no credible set. Gene windows and study participants overlap, so cases are not independent biological replicates.

- Release code: `6d60d5e5723461c3e1fc5a46fd0a0e7b6378cfa7`
- Release wheel SHA-256: `85285c26c1f6ae3caaed99c4d7766ede7f0083ea98eb2d26b7763d8654840b59`
- Release native extension SHA-256: `a9d377e45583b654ddfbe8323a783e32a61bf042c755cb26c3873f2065ed0b3e`
- Benchmark protocol SHA-256: `3893ec7f92fc042f15eade88a4c27a452835bf3285dfda037d6133c55fc56825` (hash of the protocol file as executed; the published copy was later edited only to remove host names, so its bytes differ)
- Statistical reference: R 4.4.0; susieR 0.16.6, `8e56a8e038e989856d106d9ca5175cc664fea9d2`.

Both runtime metrics use timing-instrumented copies of these release artifacts; the instrumented native binary is not byte-identical to the release wheel. The patch, derived binary hashes and timing boundaries are in the [measurement archive](https://github.com/LucaJiang/prusie-analysis/tree/main/02_benchmark/archive).

Nonconverged fits stopped at `max_iter=100`. They remain in every runtime and memory summary.

Counts come from the first retained call. Credible sets re-derived from the saved final alpha of both implementations with the susieR 0.16.6 rule contain the same variants in every case.
